_doc: Community-maintained database of game launcher quirks Carafe knows about.
When a user adds a game via GameFormSheet, the picked exe is matched against
every entry's `match` block; the first hit surfaces a 'we recognise this'
card with the option to auto-apply the entry's `fix` block into the game's
high    — Verified working by maintainers or a referenced community tool.
medium  — Partial reports; works for some users.
pending — Educated guess; needs first-hand verification. The UI shows a
warning so users know they're trying an unconfirmed config.
To add a new entry, copy an existing block, update the match + fix data,
and open a PR. See Report Compatibility button in the app for the issue
FRAGILITY: exe filenames are matched case-insensitively against the picked
URL's lastPathComponent. Folder hints scan all path components (also case-
insensitive). False positives are possible if a folder name like 'launcher'
is too generic — keep hints specific (publisher + product, not bare 'launcher').

failureSignals.message: WWM's launcher reports `not support avx`. Apple Silicon/Rosetta does not expose AVX instructions to Windows code, so this launcher may be unable to complete the game download/update on this Mac. If WWM later ships a non-AVX launcher/game build, update this profile; for now this is a hard compatibility warning rather than a missing DLL problem.

fix.notes:
⚠ DEPLOY vs _DEPLOY: WWM's installer leaves TWO launcher.exe files side-by-side — one in Win32/deploy/ (correct) and one in Win32/_deploy/ (staging leftover, missing the Qt5 DLLs). If you see Qt5Widgets.dll / Qt5Core.dll / Qt5Gui.dll / Qt5Network.dll / CrashHunter_PC3.dll / detect.dll / dxgi.dll "not found" errors, you picked the wrong one — re-add the game and navigate to Program Files/wwm/Win32/deploy/launcher.exe (no underscore). Wine's working-directory resolution is fine; both Carafe and the launcher walk up from launcher.exe's parent folder, so picking the _deploy variant means Qt5 looks for its DLLs in _deploy/ where they don't exist. Carafe now provisions Qt5Svg.dll automatically from Qt's official 5.15.2 MSVC2019 qtsvg archive and places it beside the selected launcher exe before launch.

STRONG RECOMMENDATION: skip the launcher entirely when possible. The launcher is used only for updates — once the game is downloaded, the actual game runs from Engine/Binaries/Win64r/wwm.exe (or Win64rh/wwm.exe for HK/Macau/Taiwan servers on the Steam build). The NetEase standalone install lays out differently (Program Files/wwm/...); look for wwm.exe inside the install tree and point Carafe there.

NOTE: DXVK conflicts with GPTK on the same bottle (both ship d3d11/dxgi.dll) — this profile pins graphicsBackend to D3DMetal so it's safe on either GPTK or Wine Staging bottles. If you want DXVK specifically (Wine Staging only), override per-game in the Compat sheet.

Hoyoverse's launcher uses an embedded WebKit that crashes under Wine on macOS. The YAAGL community proves direct game-exe launch works for the single-player path. Anti-cheat (mhyprot2) won't load — multiplayer modes will be blocked. If installing this game, point Carafe at GenshinImpact.exe (or StarRail.exe / honkai equivalent) inside Game/Game_Data/.

Battle.net runs under Wine 8+ on macOS once you've installed the VC++ runtimes and disabled the crash handler (which itself crashes a lot). Many Blizzard games launch through it cleanly; games gated behind kernel-level anti-cheat (Diablo IV's Warden integration, Overwatch 2's tournament mode) won't work.
